result:
The proposed answer is wrong. The n = 3 case already shows it.

For n = 3, K_3 has only one cycle, the triangle, which needs all three edges. So e_1 lies on a cycle exactly when t = 3, giving T = 3 with certainty and E[T] = 3. The proposed formula (n+1)/2 gives 2.

The error is in the reduction. The solution treats the time until u and v connect as the first success in a fixed random permutation with K = n−1 "crossing" edges. But the crossing set changes after every edge is added, because the components grow. The first-success lemma does not apply to this changing set.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 5
